items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: I worshipped Johnny Hodges you know, but it was years before I could bring myself to really tackle the alto, because he was just too far beyond.

ctx.x: Did you at the time think it valuable to pick out certain clarinet solos and really learn how to play them note for note?

Yeah. I appreciated Goodman, but he was too far beyond, it was too difficult, it was more than I could possibly comprehend. But Bechet, when I discovered Bechet, this was after I knew about Goodman, some of the things he did were simpler and I was more able to learn the solos and try to develop my own way of playing but in his style. What happened was the first time we went to the recording studio to record for Commodore I walked in the studio and Milt Gabler looks at me and I just had my clarinet and he says,…

That’s a pretty mature attitude I think, at that young age, for someone who in your eyes probably was a pretty powerful record man, and he’s saying bring that horn, and you’re going, I’m not ready to do that yet.
